question: Will Eritrea expel Ethiopia's diplomats in return, yes or no?

lines.text: Ethiopia is expelling ten Eritrean diplomats.
lines.note: Ethiopian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 1 Oct 2026

lines.text: Its foreign ministry says it is also closing its embassy in Asmara, Eritrea's capital.
The ten diplomats have forty-eight hours to leave.
lines.note: Declared persona non grata (Xinhua, Eastleigh Voice)

lines.text: The ministry accuses Eritrea of direct and indirect acts of hostility and belligerence.

scene.quote: direct and indirect acts of hostility and belligerence

lines.text: It says the diplomats pose a direct threat to national security.
Eritrea denies backing the rebel alliance fighting Ethiopia's government, the Jerusalem Post reports.
It follows blasts overnight in Addis Ababa, hours after drones were banned over the city.
lines.note: AP via WSLS; BBC; Bloomberg, 1 Oct 2026

lines.text: An alliance source told Reuters it carried out drone strikes. Reuters could not verify that.
lines.note: Reuters via Jerusalem Post and Eastleigh Voice

lines.text: In the north, fighting has returned to Tigray, including around Mekelle.
lines.note: Jerusalem Post; Al Jazeera: conflict widens in the north

lines.text: A sharp reversal. Ethiopia reopened this embassy in 2018, after a peace deal that won Abiy Ahmed the Nobel Peace Prize.
lines.note: Jerusalem Post, Dawan; Al Jazeera 6 Sep 2018

lines.text: The two neighbours fought a border war from 1998 to 2000.
Ethiopia says it remains committed to the peaceful resolution of disputes.

scene.quote: committed to the peaceful resolution of disputes

lines.text: Embassy shut, diplomats out. Will Eritrea expel Ethiopia's diplomats in return, yes or no?

caption: Ethiopia shuts its Eritrea embassy: the foreign ministry is closing its embassy in Asmara and has given 10 Eritrean diplomats 48 hours to leave. It follows blasts heard overnight in Addis Ababa. Will Eritrea expel Ethiopia's diplomats in return, yes or no?
notes_full: Announcement 1 Oct 2026 by Ethiopia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs; first reports about 15:00 UTC (Addis Insight 15:14, JPost 15:19, Garowe 15:20, Firstpost 15:43, Anadolu 15:59, Reuters 16:23, DW 16:59)

Verbatim: 'in response to Eritrea's direct and indirect acts of hostility and belligerence against Ethiopia'; diplomats persona non grata 'for involvement in activities that pose a direct threat to Ethiopia's national security in breach of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations'; 'committed to the peaceful resolution of disputes' (Xinhua)
48 hours to leave (Xinhua, Eastleigh Voice, Dawan)
Eritrea denies supporting the opposition alliance (JPost)

Blasts in Addis Ababa night of 30 Sep to 1 Oct after NISS banned drones over Addis and surroundings; intelligence official confirmed three blasts in three locations; unclear if attack or training (AP)
Alliance source to Reuters: several drone strikes incl. military HQ; Reuters could not verify; PM office, government, military did not respond (JPost, Eastleigh Voice)
Embassy reopened Sep 2018 (Al Jazeera); Abiy Nobel Peace Prize 2019; border war 1998-2000
Left out: the alliance's stated aim regarding the PM (regime-change framing), any casualty figures, any Ethiopia-Eritrea war speculation
